Analyzes conventional commits since the last release to determine the next
version, generate a changelog, and create or update a release PR/MR.

When a merged release PR/MR is waiting with the pending autorelease label,
this command first creates the tag/release from the latest changelog entry and
marks the PR/MR as tagged.

Settings resolve in priority order: command-line flag, then the .yeet.yaml
config file, then the built-in default. A .yeet.yaml file is required (run
"yeet init" to create one).

Authentication tokens are read only from environment variables, never from
flags or config:
  GitHub:       GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN (optional GITHUB_URL for Enterprise)
  GitLab:       GITLAB_TOKEN or GL_TOKEN (optional GITLAB_URL for self-hosted)
  Azure DevOps: AZURE_DEVOPS_SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN or AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT
                (optional AZURE_DEVOPS_URL)

Commit history is read from the local git checkout. The checkout must be
complete (not shallow) and match the remote release branch.

Usage:
  yeet release [flags]

Examples:
  yeet release --dry-run
  yeet release --target api --target web --dry-run
  yeet release --channel beta
  yeet release --auto-merge
  yeet release --provider github --owner platform --repo yeet --dry-run

Flags:
      --auto-merge                 automatically merge the release PR/MR and finalize the release in the same run
      --auto-merge-force           attempt auto-merge while bypassing yeet readiness checks. Draft status and conflicts still block merging. Provider rules may still apply
      --auto-merge-method string   merge method for auto-merge: auto|squash|rebase|merge (defaults to the configured method, or auto if unset)
      --channel string             run a configured prerelease channel, defaulting to the channel matching the current branch
      --config string              path to config file (default: nearest ancestor .yeet.yaml)
      --dry-run                    show the planned release without creating a PR/MR
  -h, --help                       help for release
      --host string                override repository host, such as github.com or gitlab.company.com (github, gitlab, azuredevops)
      --owner string               override repository owner or namespace (github)
      --project string             override full project path, including subgroups (github, gitlab, azuredevops)
      --provider string            override provider: auto|github|gitlab|azuredevops
      --remote string              override git remote used for repository auto-detection
      --repo string                override repository name (github, azuredevops)
      --target stringArray         limit analysis to one or more configured targets (repeatable)

Global Flags:
      --no-color   disable colored output
      --quiet      show warnings and errors only
  -v, --verbose    enable debug logging
